analysis:
This PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The visible change is lines 453-473, a new bullet describing how a stop request ends cluster onboarding on the leader and the joining Mac. It documents a stop counter (ClusterSetupRecord.stopsAsked, ClusterControlReply.stopsAsked), a leader step mark (ClusterOnboardingLeaderStep.stopsBefore), and a compare-under-command-lock rule (OnboardingLive.localServe(unlessStoppedSince:)). No code, endpoint, key, attestation, or encryption behavior changes in the supplied evidence, so I found no regression against TB-002/TB-011 or the prefix-cache threat T-041.

The documented behavior is a local control and onboarding lifecycle on the authenticated pair control link. Two points are worth tracking, but neither is established as a regression by this docs-only diff:
1. Availability: a stop request from either Mac ends the onboarding. The text says the joining Mac trusts the leader's reported count, and that the count is nil from older builds and then ignored. Whether the count is bound to the authenticated member identity depends on the unseen code (ClusterControlReply, ClusterOnboardingFollowedStop). The line 415 text says fresh peer facts are used only while the authenticated member identity matches.
2. The docs mention a stop racing a registration and says the leader neither registers nor restarts a pair stopped since its start. That is a lifecycle guard in unseen code, not a documented trust change.

The other prose in the units (the Nemotron Super and DevNet build-isolation passages) is unchanged context. The excerpt ends at line 806, so the later part of the file was not visible. The patch excerpt is truncated, and the head ranges 3239-3286 are outside the supplied text. Those lines could not be examined, which is a coverage limit. The implementation of the stop-count logic is not supplied, so a follow-up pass should confirm the count is authenticated and monotonic and that the compare-and-set under the command lock holds.
